supported_fuse_arrangement.mechanism: FSTYP=fuse + FUSE_SUBTYP=<suffix> and a /sbin/mount.fuse.<suffix> mount helper; TEST_DEV / SCRATCH_DEV are dummy names (e.g. non1/non2), not block devices

blockers: xfstests does not run or even configure until its own helper binaries are built (`make`), which requires libtool plus acl/attr/uuid/cap development libraries; `./check` refuses to start without `fsstress`.

There is no built-in `FSTYP` for FUSE or for OrFS. The only documented FUSE substrate (README.fuse) pairs `FSTYP=fuse` with `FUSE_SUBTYP` and a `/sbin/mount.fuse.<subtype>` mount helper, and it is written for libfuse's `passthrough_ll` example.
OrFS's mount model is a foreground daemon (`orfs mount <backing> <mnt>`); it provides no `/sbin/mount.fuse.orfs` helper, so the kernel's userland-mount path used by `FSTYP=fuse` has nothing to call.

The generic tests overwhelmingly use `xfs_io` (from xfsprogs) and assume block-device semantics (block-granular fallocate/punch-hole, mkfs, FS_IOC ioctls) that an append-only FUSE filesystem does not expose.
conclusion: xfstests cannot be run against a mounted OrFS volume in this environment. Its FUSE substrate exists but targets the libfuse passthrough example and requires (a) building xfstests' helper tools, (b) xfsprogs, and (c) an OrFS mount helper the project does not provide. No results are fabricated. POSIX behaviour is instead exercised by the pjdfstest court (evidence/correctness/pjdfstest.json) and the custom mounted model court (evidence/correctness/posix-results.json).
